title: Microsoft Purview: catalogue, lineage and classification

videos.script: A customer writes to Quitanda. Under Brazil's data protection law, she asks for every piece of data the company holds about her. {{request}} Somebody has to answer within days. Where is her CPF? In the orders database, yes. In the nightly export, probably. In a notebook somebody copied last spring, maybe. {{where}} Nobody knows, because nobody wrote it down. That is the problem a catalogue solves. {{catalogue}} Microsoft Purview scans the stores you register and builds a map of what is in them. It recognises columns that hold CPFs, e-mail addresses and phone numbers, and labels them. {{scan}} It also draws lineage: which pipeline copied which table into which file. {{lineage}} Purview has no emulator. So you will write a small classifier of your own and run it over Quitanda's export in Azurite, to see what a classifier does and where it goes wrong. {{classifier}} Then you will see what Purview charges for keeping the map. {{bill}}
